description: Ultradian pulse train and downstream transcription model: does CBG loss increase free cortisol variability and reduce GR transcriptional output?
code:
import numpy as np, matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.integrate import solve_ivp

Kd, K_ALB, Vp, CL = 30.0, 3.4, 3.5, 25.0/4.4   # CL referenced to (free+albumin)
S0 = CL*10*(1+K_ALB)                            # basal secretion -> 10 nmol/L free

def simulate(Bmax, S_func, T=24., n=24001, KdR=5.0, k_tx=1.5):
    """State: [free cortisol, GR-driven transcript]. Transcript is produced in
    proportion to fractional GR occupancy and degraded first-order (k_tx /h),
    i.e. a low-pass filter on occupancy - the standard way a slow genomic
    readout integrates a hormone pulse."""
    def g(F):    return (1+K_ALB)+Bmax*Kd/(Kd+F)**2
    def elim(F): return CL*F*(1+K_ALB)
    F0 = S0/(CL*(1+K_ALB)); R0 = (F0/(KdR+F0))
    def rhs(t,y):
        F=max(y[0],0.0)
        return [(S_func(t)-elim(F))/(Vp*g(F)), k_tx*(F/(KdR+F) - y[1])]
    ts=np.linspace(0,T,n)
    s=solve_ivp(rhs,(0,T),[F0,R0],t_eval=ts,rtol=1e-8,atol=1e-10,max_step=0.02)
    return ts, s.y[0], s.y[1]

# ---------------- A. ULTRADIAN PULSE TRAIN ----------------
# Adrenal secretion in vivo is pulsatile (~1 pulse/h). CBG buffers these pulses;
# without it, free cortisol should track each pulse directly.
def pulse_train(t, period=1.0, width=0.12, amp=8.0):
    ph = t % period
    return S0*(1.0 + (amp-1.0)*np.exp(-0.5*((ph-0.3)/width)**2))

ts, Fw, Rw = simulate(700.0, pulse_train)
_,  Fk, Rk = simulate(0.0,   pulse_train)
sel = ts > 6.0   # discard transient
def stats(F):
    f=F[sel]; return f.mean(), f.std(), f.std()/f.mean(), f.max()-f.min()
mw, sw, cvw, rw_ = stats(Fw); mk, sk, cvk, rk_ = stats(Fk)
print("=== A. Ultradian pulsatility of FREE cortisol (1 pulse/h, 8-fold secretion pulses) ===")
print(f"{'':14s}{'mean':>8s}{'SD':>8s}{'CV':>8s}{'peak-trough':>13s}")
print(f"{'CBG normal':14s}{mw:8.2f}{sw:8.2f}{cvw:8.3f}{rw_:13.2f}")
print(f"{'CBG null':14s}{mk:8.2f}{sk:8.2f}{cvk:8.3f}{rk_:13.2f}")
print(f"  mean free ratio null/normal     = {mk/mw:.4f}")
print(f"  CV ratio null/normal            = {cvk/cvw:.2f}")
print(f"  peak-to-trough ratio null/normal= {rk_/rw_:.2f}")

# ---------------- B. TRANSCRIPTIONAL OUTPUT vs READOUT SPEED ----------------
print("\n=== B. Integrated GR transcriptional output during a single stress episode ===")
def stress(t, t0=0.5, dur=0.5, mult=6., tau=0.33):
    if t<t0: return S0
    if t<t0+dur: return S0*mult
    return S0*(1+(mult-1)*np.exp(-(t-t0-dur)/tau))
print(f"{'readout half-life':>20s}{'k_tx (/h)':>11s}{'receptor Kd':>13s}"
      f"{'output AUC ratio null/normal':>30s}")
rows=[]
for KdR in [0.5, 5.0, 20.0]:
    for k_tx,lab in [(6.0,'7 min'),(1.5,'28 min'),(0.35,'2 h'),(0.087,'8 h')]:
        t,Fw2,Rw2 = simulate(700.0, stress, KdR=KdR, k_tx=k_tx)
        _,Fk2,Rk2 = simulate(0.0,   stress, KdR=KdR, k_tx=k_tx)
        r = np.trapz(Rk2-Rk2[0],t)/np.trapz(Rw2-Rw2[0],t)
        rows.append((KdR,lab,k_tx,r))
        print(f"{lab:>20s}{k_tx:11.3f}{KdR:13.1f}{r:30.3f}")
print("  free cortisol AUC ratio is 1.0000 in every one of these runs")

# ---------------- figure ----------------
fig,ax=plt.subplots(1,3,figsize=(15,4.3))
m=(ts>=8)&(ts<=14)
ax[0].plot(ts[m],Fw[m],lw=2,color='#2b6cb0',label='CBG normal')
ax[0].plot(ts[m],Fk[m],lw=2,color='#b2283c',label='CBG null')
ax[0].set_xlabel('time (h)'); ax[0].set_ylabel('free cortisol (nmol/L)')
ax[0].set_title(f'Ultradian pulses: same mean free cortisol,\n{cvk/cvw:.1f}x larger swings without CBG')
ax[0].legend(frameon=False)
t,Fw2,Rw2 = simulate(700.0, stress, KdR=5.0, k_tx=0.35)
_,Fk2,Rk2 = simulate(0.0,   stress, KdR=5.0, k_tx=0.35)
mm=t<=8
ax[1].plot((t[mm]-.5),Rw2[mm],lw=2,color='#2b6cb0',label='CBG normal')
ax[1].plot((t[mm]-.5),Rk2[mm],lw=2,color='#b2283c',label='CBG null')
ax[1].set_xlabel('time from stress onset (h)'); ax[1].set_ylabel('GR-driven transcript (a.u.)')
ax[1].set_title('Slow genomic readout (2 h half-life,\nGR Kd 5 nM) is blunted in the null')
ax[1].legend(frameon=False)
labs=['7 min','28 min','2 h','8 h']
for KdR,c in [(0.5,'#1a365d'),(5.0,'#2b6cb0'),(20.0,'#90cdf4')]:
    v=[r[3] for r in rows if r[0]==KdR]
    ax[2].plot(labs,v,'o-',lw=2,color=c,label=f'receptor Kd {KdR:g} nM')
ax[2].axhline(1,color='grey',ls='--',lw=1)
ax[2].set_xlabel('half-life of the downstream readout')
ax[2].set_ylabel('output AUC, null / normal')
ax[2].set_title('Deficit appears only in slow,\nhigh-affinity readouts'); ax[2].legend(frameon=False)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
